summary: A 90-foot WPA-built Aermotor steel fire tower in Tippecanoe River State Park, Indiana, open to visitors to climb via a quarter-mile trail.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7x7 ft cab

access.note: Open for visitors to climb, via about a quarter-mile trail from the parking area in Tippecanoe River State Park.

visit.trail_note: About a 0.25 mile hike from the parking area to the tower.

events.note: Built by Works Progress Administration labor in Tippecanoe River State Park, per the National Historic Lookout Register.
An alternate source dates completion of the WPA-built steel tower to 1940.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register (US 975) on September 1, 2013.

evidence.supports: built 1937 by WPA, 90ft Aermotor, open to climb
evidence.quote: Constructed by the Works Progress Administration in 1937 within Indiana's Tippecanoe River State Park, Winamac Fire Tower is a 90' Aermotor with a 7'x7' cab. Reached by a quarter-mile trail, it is open for visitors to climb.
Park Ranger directed us to the tower; about a 0.25 mile hike from the parking area.

evidence.supports: 1940 completion date and WPA labor, location in Tippecanoe State Park
evidence.quote: 1940: A steel fire tower was completed by the use of Works Progress Administration labor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The National Historic Lookout Register gives 1937 while a separate eastern-U.S. lookout history page gives 1940 for the same WPA-built steel tower in Tippecanoe River State Park. The story reports 1937 as the primary date and flags the three-year discrepancy.

notes_for_editor: NHLR is a solid primary source with direct site-visit detail (trail distance, ranger anecdote, climbable status). The weebly compendium corroborates WPA construction and park location but differs on the year by three years; could not resolve which is more authoritative within budget. No source addresses overnight rental, so the story states the absence of any such record rather than asserting it is unavailable.
